_comment: Rules the API enforces and the web app previews. Data, not code, for the reason given in index.js: the API requires CommonJS and the web app is bundled as ESM, and JSON is the one thing both read natively. Each side builds its own validator from these values, so the rule is written once even though it runs twice. Patterns are regex SOURCE strings; every one needs the 'u' flag.

name.patternComment: A name starts with a letter and ends with a letter or a combining mark. In between it may also carry spaces, hyphens and apostrophes - straight or curly, because phone keyboards produce the curly one. \p{L} covers every script, so this accepts محمد, Владимир and José as readily as it accepts Ali. It rejects digits, @, <, /, emoji, a NUL byte, and anything else that is not part of a human name. The final character was once required to be \p{L}, which quietly rejected most Indic names: Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil and Telugu words routinely end in a dependent vowel sign, and that sign is \p{M}. किराया, বাড়ি, வாடகை and ఇంటి అద్దె were all refused. A name may still not END in a space, hyphen or apostrophe.

messages.pattern: Name can only contain letters, spaces, hyphens, and apostrophes.

email.patternComment: Deliberately permissive about the local part and strict about the shape: exactly one @, something on each side, at least one dot in the domain, and no whitespace anywhere. Tighter patterns are how valid addresses get rejected - plus-addressing, apostrophes and long TLDs are all legitimate. Real deliverability is proved by sending mail, not by a regex.

messages.pattern: Enter a valid email address, like you@university.edu
messages.tooLong: That email address is too long

password.maxLengthComment: bcrypt silently ignores everything past 72 bytes, so accepting more would let a student believe in a strength the hash never sees.

requirements.label: No spaces at the start or end

password.requirementsComment: Unicode classes rather than [A-Z]/[a-z]/[0-9], so a password written in another script is judged by the same rules. 'special' is anything that is not a letter or a digit, which includes a space in the middle - deliberately, because a passphrase is a good password. noEdgeSpace ends in .+ rather than .*, so an empty box shows nothing ticked: a green mark against a password nobody has typed reads as progress that has not happened.

messages.tooLong: Password must be 72 characters or fewer

terms.message: Please accept the terms to create your account
